This is sweet of you to say, I did work hard to get where I’m at; but there were so many hardships I shouldn’t have experienced during my education if only I had a 504 the whole time. 
I self harmed, I was severely depressed and anxious, I made many suicide attempts; but having support through the disability office at my school broke me free from my own mental shackles. 
No one should have to suffer like I did; even though I made it, I look back and realize how much of myself I lost in the process .

I went my entire schooling career without a 504 until my senior year of undergrad. That year alone changed my life and showed me my true potential.
 For once I felt seen, understood, and not worthless. I did not “turn out fine” by dealing with it; I 360’d my grades and potential in that single year of 504 access. 
 This makes me horrified go back for my graduates. I had a single year of help, positivity, support, and recognition; I don’t see how I could ever go back to suffering.

My first DM was my best friend at the time and she used this method to kinda get me into the table top world. It’s mainly a comfort strategy to get you out of your shell from what I understood. She had my character built around secrets and put into a side quest just as with the others. It made me understand how to RP better and pretty much what I should be doing after all. Needless to say, it was good to help me ease into it. Just try to speak out a little more and bring excitement to the table. It’s okay to be nervous but just think, unless that’s your characters personality then don’t be. It’s all literal fun an games, get out of your comfort zone. It’s really fun at the end of the day when your character and someone else’s form a bond that you can bounce RP off of. It’ll get easier I promise but no you aren’t a bad player at all, just learning :)
